segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Hello, and welcome back to Imagination Nights. [pause 3]

Settle into the bed. Pull the covers up to where you like them. [pause 8]

Take one deep breath, and let it go with a sigh. [pause 8]

Now let your breathing find its own pace. You do not have to control it. Just notice it. [pause 10]

Feel your feet getting heavy. Your legs. Your back sinking into the mattress. [pause 10]

Now let us relax the body, one part at a time. You do not have to do anything. Just notice each part as I name it, and let it get heavy. [pause 8]

Your feet. Let them be warm and heavy. [pause 15]

Your calves and your knees. Heavy. [pause 15]

Your hips and your lower back. Let them sink. [pause 15]

Your belly. Let it rise and fall on its own. [pause 15]

Your chest. Your shoulders. Your arms, all the way down to your fingertips. [pause 15]

Your neck. Your face. The little muscles around your eyes. [pause 15]

Your whole body, heavy and warm, held by the bed. [pause 15]

The day is finished. This part of the night is yours. [pause 8]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Tonight's scene is about a trip. Somewhere you have wanted to go. Maybe the ocean. Maybe a city. Maybe the town where your grandparents were born. [pause 13]

A trip is a good wish to practice with, because the details are so easy to feel. Sand. Wind. A new street. Food that tastes different. [pause 15]

Instead of picturing the planning and the packing, we picture being there, on the third or fourth day, when you have already relaxed into it. [pause 15]

You do not have to know how the trip would happen. That is daytime work. Tonight is only for the feeling of having arrived, of being rested and unhurried. [pause 15]

Let the place be as real as you can make it. Picture the weather, the sounds of the language people speak there, the shoes you are wearing. Small details make the scene feel like a memory instead of a wish. And memories are restful. [pause 5]

As always, this is imagination, not a promise. Even if the trip stays a dream for now, the rest you feel tonight is real. [pause 20]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
You wake up in a room that is not your own, and for a second you do not know where you are. Then you remember, and you smile. [pause 30]

Open the curtains. Notice what is outside. Water. Hills. Rooftops. [pause 30]

Step outside. Feel the air on your face. It smells different here. Salt, or pine, or bread from a bakery. [pause 30]

Walk slowly. You have nowhere to be. Your phone is in your pocket, quiet. [pause 30]

Find a place to sit. A bench. A wall. A patch of sand. Watch people going about their morning. [pause 33]

Taste something new. Let it surprise you. [pause 30]

Notice that your shoulders are lower than they have been in months. [pause 33]

Later, the light turns gold. You are tired in the good way, from walking and looking. [pause 33]

Back in the room, you lie down, and through the window you hear the sounds of this place settling into night. [pause 35]

Say in your mind, I came. I am here. [pause 35]

Let those far-off sounds become the sounds around you now. [pause 35]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
We will end here for tonight. [pause 10]

Keep the feeling, not the effort. Let the effort go. [pause 15]

Whatever happens tomorrow, tonight you practiced feeling at peace. That is worth something on its own. [pause 20]

Let sleep come when it comes. There is no rush. [pause 20]

Notice the weight of the covers. The cool side of the pillow. The dark. [pause 25]

Let each breath out be a little longer than the one before. [pause 25]

Nothing more to picture. Nothing more to try. Only rest. [pause 30]

Good night. [pause 60]
